sections.title: Unruly Bodies, Contested Spaces: Race, Gender, and the Politics of Schooling
sections.description: How do schools teach us which bodies belong and which are marked unruly for disrupting the order of things? Unruly Bodies, Contested Spaces examines K–12 schooling as a key site where racial, gender, and class order is taught, enforced, and challenged. From dress codes and discipline to bathrooms and curriculum, schools’ culture and policies have historically signaled which bodies and behaviors are rendered normal/abnormal, safe/dangerous, and aligned/disruptive. In the wake of continued battles over gender-affirming care, censorship, equity, and the role of public education, this course will ask how these political struggles are lived in the everyday spaces and lives of schooling. Grounded in women of color feminisms, trans studies, queer theory, and geographies, we will use theoretical, legislative, and literary texts to examine how youth navigate, refuse, and dream beyond the terms schools set for them. What might their unruliness reveal about the limits and possibilities of schooling in the past, present, and future?
